$comment: Created after interpretation.v18 and grounding.v8 were frozen, 17 September 2026. Not run: Gemini project monthly spend cap reached. Separate from the release gate and the original reserved fresh set. Each conversation has three substantive follow-ups so its cost can describe an actual full conversation. Do not tune prompts to this file and still call it unseen.

conversations.question: I share an allotment with two neighbours. They want more wildflowers and I want to grow vegetables. I want to understand our different aims before we decide what to plant.

turns.text: How do care and fairness fit together when we want different things from the same space?
We have now agreed to split the beds equally, but we still haven't decided what sharing the work would mean. How does that change the reading?
What different meanings of a fair share could we consider without assuming one of us is selfish?

conversations.question: My father died last year. I found a recording of him reading a story, and I feel both glad to have it and sad when I listen. I want to understand that mixture, not change it.

turns.text: How can gladness and sadness both belong here without one being the more truthful feeling?
I don't listen often, and that is deliberate. Can we look at the meaning of having the recording without suggesting that I listen more?
Where does hope fit in this reading if I am not asking for the sadness to disappear?
